disclaimer: This explains your report in plain words. It is not a diagnosis and not medical advice. Only your doctor can tell you what these results mean for you.

note.what: Red cell distribution width, or RDW, measures how much your red blood cells differ from one another in size and volume.
note.ask: What do my RDW and MCV results mean when read together with the rest of my blood count?
note.source: MedlinePlus, National Library of Medicine (US) — https://medlineplus.gov/lab-tests/red-blood-cell-rbc-indices/ (updated 7 October 2024)
note.means: A result outside the range means there are differences in the size of your red blood cells; on its own this is not enough for a diagnosis.

note.what: Haemoglobin is the iron-rich protein in red blood cells that carries oxygen; this test measures how much of it is in your blood.
note.ask: What could be causing my haemoglobin result, and do I need follow-up tests such as iron or vitamin B-12 levels?
note.source: MedlinePlus, National Library of Medicine (US) — https://medlineplus.gov/lab-tests/hemoglobin-test/ (updated 27 October 2024)
note.means: A lower result can be a sign of anaemia, low iron or vitamin B-12, thalassaemia, blood loss or liver disease.

note.what: Mean corpuscular volume, or MCV, is the average size of your red blood cells.
note.ask: What do my MCV and other red cell results mean together, and do I need tests for iron or vitamin levels?
note.source: MedlinePlus, National Library of Medicine (US) — https://medlineplus.gov/lab-tests/red-blood-cell-rbc-indices/ (updated 7 October 2024)
note.means: A lower MCV, meaning smaller cells, can be a sign of iron deficiency anaemia or of thalassaemia, an inherited blood disorder.

note.what: This test shows what share of your blood is made up of red blood cells, the cells that carry oxygen around your body.
note.ask: What level is normal for me given my age, sex, smoking and altitude, and do I need a full blood count or iron tests?
note.source: MedlinePlus, National Library of Medicine (US) — https://medlineplus.gov/lab-tests/hematocrit-test/ (updated 25 November 2024)
note.means: A lower result can be a sign of anaemia or blood loss, and is also commonly seen in pregnancy because of the extra fluid in the body.
